page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-80 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on Intel Xeon scalable x86_64 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Configured with 40 physical cores and 80 dedicated vCPUs via multithreading, it provides 80 GB of system memory, maintaining a tight 1 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 33 MB of shared L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage and requires attached persistent disks for all data retention, and it does not feature hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong parallel compute and memory throughput metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 52,249.76 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 75,231.71, placing it in the top quartile of multi-threaded compute workloads. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaches 205.69 GB/sec, while cached read bandwidth measures 4,123.03 GB/sec. Synthetic database benchmarks show robust performance, reaching 22,461.59 operations in PassMark database tests and 73.83 million operations per second in Redis SET routines. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1,159) and stress-ng single-core (1,838.89) settle in the middle tiers.

Given its minimal 1 GB RAM per vCPU allocation and lack of integrated storage, the instance presents an efficient multi-core CPU capacity without the cost overhead of unutilized memory pools. However, memory-intensive datasets or models that demand significant memory footprints per thread will encounter bottlenecks, as reflected by modest LLM text generation rates. Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-80 is well suited for highly parallelized batch processing, media encoding, distributed compilation pipelines, static web traffic handling, and horizontally scaled compute workers where raw multi-core throughput takes precedence over per-core memory capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-80 is a high-density, compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. It delivers 80 dedicated vCPUs across 40 physical cores paired with 80 GB of RAM, yielding a 1 GB per core memory footprint. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI alongside 33 MB of L3 cache, with no integrated local storage or hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compute throughput, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 75,231.71, PassMark CPU extended instructions reaching 65,069.43, and uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 205 GB/sec. While single-thread execution rates and per-core memory are moderate, its high thread density provides qualitative resource efficiency for parallel workloads. The configuration is optimal for continuous integration builds, distributed batch processing, parallel data transformation, and compute-heavy worker nodes.
